newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister to visit Iraq for economic talks.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister to visit Iraq for economic talks.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Ahmet Cemil Tunc will go to Iraq at the weekend at the invitation of Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed, his press office said on Thursday.

It said Tunc would also meet Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf, Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh and several other officials during his visit on March 30-April 4.
Tunc will be accompanied by several officials from the energy, transport and housing ministries, it said.
His office did not give details on the contents of the visit but a press official said the talks would "dwell on bilateral economic and energy matters".
Turkey's state oil refinery Tupras has a contract to lift 75,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude from Baghdad's U.N.-controlled sales under an oil-for-food deal.
Last week some Turkish companies began selling pulses and vegetable oil to Iraq as the first shipments of food items under the U.N. deal.

Rasheed came to Turkey in December and discussed several projects between the two neighbours including one on Iraq's gas sales to Turkey through a pipeline after an exploration of gas fields in Iraq by Turkish oil company TPAO, pipeline concern Botas and the Iraqi government.
